newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX reverses as holiday mood hits sentiment.
newsitem.headline: German DAX reverses as holiday mood hits sentiment.

text.p: The DAX index of 30 German blue-chip shares went for a rollercoaster ride on Wednesday during a session which saw the DAX hit records at 3,695.31 points and then plummet to end down over one percentage point.

Floor trade closed with the DAX at 3,636,42 points, down 37.94 points or 1.03 percent. Dealers said that the market consolidated after it failed to breach the psychologically important threshold at 3,700 points.

Dealers also said that a regional holiday on Thursday meant that traders were unwilling to take up new positions in the market ahead of what would turn into a long weekend for many market players, who would take Friday off as well.
Weakness on the German debt market was also playing on market nerves.

Among the features was insurance giant Allianz AG Holding, which rose to new highs after it said it expected its premium income to rise around 11 percent to around 83 billion marks in 1997 and said it expected moderate double-digit growth in 1997.
Allianz fell back along with the rest of the market to end the day down 3.30 marks at 372.50 marks.
Industrial gaint Daimler Benz AG also scaled new heights in electronic trade earlier on, after it said it expected "substantial" increases in 1997 sales and operating profits.
The share rose to a high of 137.45 marks at one point in electronic trade but also fell back to end the session down 50 pfennigs at 135.90 marks.
